facility.name: Kimble Learning Center
facility.programs_provided: School Age Care,Meals Provided ,After School Care,Snacks Provided,Drop-In Care,Part Time Care,Transportation to/from School ,Field Trips

provenance.note: Census Geocoder Non_Exact match: 2200 E 10TH AVE, AMARILLO, TX, 79102

inspection_summary.note: Texas HHSC inspections, report investigations and assessments since October 2017, updated daily.

occurrences.finding: Required Immunizations: A child's file that was reviewed during the inspection did not have a current immunization record on file.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Immunizations (26 TAC §746.613(a))

occurrences.finding: Naptime for Infants: An infant was showing noticeable signs being tired and grabbing at the rails of their crib. The caregiver told the child that they know the child is tired but they have at least an hour before they can lay down. The child then began pushing and biting other children due to being tired and requiring rest.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Naptime for Infants (26 TAC §746.2423)

occurrences.finding: Activities for Infants - Not in Restrictive Device for more than 15 Minutes: An infant was observed in a restrictive device for more than 15 minutes.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Activities for Infants - Not in Restrictive Device for more than 15 Minutes (26 TAC §746.2417(2)(B))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling: A caregiver was observed at inspection grabbing a child by the arm with enough pressure to leave an impression on the child's arm and remained visiible for five minutes.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling (26 TAC §746.2805(3))

occurrences.finding: Requirements during probation: One staff member did not have health and safety training as specified in condition 2 of the operation's probation within 10 days of their hire date.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Requirements during probation (26 TAC §745.8641)

occurrences.finding: Toys and Equipment to be Sanitized Set Aside: Toys were observed being cleaned up and placed back on the shelves. Toys that had been in the children's mouths were mixed with the clean toys that were placed back on the shelves for children to access.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Toys and Equipment to be Sanitized Set Aside (26 TAC §746.3407(1))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: Two caregivers were in the classroom but were not maintaining awareness of the ongoing activities of the children they were responsible for. One child was laying on the floor with their pants partially down and exposing themself and touching themself. A caregiver walked past the child and then continued picking up toys without intervening.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Toys and Equipment to be Sanitized Set Aside: Toddlers were observed playing with a group of toys on the carpet and toys were continuously placed in their mouth and then placed back in the group of other toys and then another child would pick up the contaminated toy and then place in their mouth.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Toys and Equipment to be Sanitized Set Aside (26 TAC §746.3407(1))

occurrences.finding: Children Handwashing After Toileting or Diapering: One child had a potty accident and had their wet clothes changed and they did not have their hands washed after. Additionally, the caregiver did not wash their hands after handling the soiled clothes. Additional children had their diaper changed and some of the children did not have their hands washed after. The caregiver also did not wash her hands after each diaper change.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children Handwashing After Toileting or Diapering (26 TAC §746.3417(3))

occurrences.finding: Diapering Procedures - Sanitizing Diaper Changing Area: Multiple children's diapers were changed and the diaper changing surface was not observed being sanitized after any of the diaper changes.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Diapering Procedures - Sanitizing Diaper Changing Area (26 TAC §746.3505(e))

occurrences.finding: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Transportation training: Transportation training is not current for any current staff that transport children in care and the director of the operation additionally requires transportation training.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Transportation training (26 TAC §746.1301(a)(7)(A))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Relate to Children: A caregiver was observed at inspection telling children that if they acted like babies then they would have them and their belongings sent down to the baby room. The caregiver was not communicating with the children in a manner that treated them with courtesy and respect.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Relate to Children (26 TAC §746.1201(2))

occurrences.finding: Nutrition and Food Service - Food not a reward: A caregiver was observed at inspection telling children that they would get candy for good behavior and if they dd not listen then they would not get any.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Nutrition and Food Service - Food not a reward (26 TAC §746.3301(h))

occurrences.finding: Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Brief Supervised Separation: A caregiver had a child sit inactive for a length of time that was inappropriate for his age. The child should have been limited to 3 minutes of time out but instead was sitting for 20 minutes before being allowed to get up and participate in an activity.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Brief Supervised Separation (26 TAC §746.2803(4)(D))

occurrences.finding: Furnishings and Equipment for Toddlers - Items Accessible to Children: The toddler classroom had majority of the shelves turned towards the wall and the toys were inaccessible to children in care. This was observed during morning activities with 1.5 hour of time prior to nap time. Two music based toys were made accessible after the initial observations but the shelves that were faced away were not turned with available toys during the duration of the inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Furnishings and Equipment for Toddlers - Items Accessible to Children (26 TAC §746.2505(3))

occurrences.finding: Care Requirements for Toddlers - Holding and Comforting: Both staff members were hyper focused on other job duties, such as hand washing practices, that when multiple children had a minor injury and upset, they did not comfort them or evaluate their level of injury.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Care Requirements for Toddlers - Holding and Comforting (26 TAC §746.2501(4))

occurrences.finding: Naptime Child/Caregiver Ratio: One classroom with 21 children had reduced ratios during nap time with one caregiver. The specified age group is three year olds with children ranging from 18 month olds to  4 year olds. There was not an additional employee available in the building upon arrival at inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Naptime Child/Caregiver Ratio (26 TAC §746.1613(b))

occurrences.finding: Safety - Areas Free From Hazards: Based on the evidence obtained during the investigation, the infant classroom was not free of hazards. A container of hot soup was in reach of an infant that led to an injury that required medical treatment.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety - Areas Free From Hazards (26 TAC §746.3701)

occurrences.finding: Activities for Infants - Not in Restrictive Device for more than 15 Minutes: An infant was in a restrictive device for over 15 minutes and the director had to prompt the staff member to transition the child. It was corrected with the infant removed from the restrictive device.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Activities for Infants - Not in Restrictive Device for more than 15 Minutes (26 TAC §746.2417(2)(B))

occurrences.finding: Sign-in and Sign-out Tracking System: None of the four infants were signed in on the sign in sheet in the infant classroom. Additionally, a child for the two's classroom was not signed in either. This was corrected with the director signing the children into care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Sign-in and Sign-out Tracking System (26 TAC §746.631(a))

occurrences.finding: Posting Requirements - List entitled "Current Employees"--sized at least 81/2 X 11 inches, printed legibly, include employee first and last name: The staff list that is posted for parents was not current. Several new staff transitioned to the operation and staff also left employment from the operation and the list has not been updated. This was corrected at inspection with the staff list being updated and posted.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Posting Requirements - List entitled "Current Employees"--sized at least 81/2 X 11 inches, printed legibly, include employee first and last name (26 TAC §746.401(9))

occurrences.finding: Director's Absence -  Employees Know Who Is in Charge: During the intial walk through of the inspection, the director was absent and the staff were not aware of whom was in charge during her absence. One staff member stated the assistant director was in charge but the assistant director was present in the building to be in charge at that time. Another staff member was not aware that the director was not present in the building and stated she didn't know whom was in charge.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Director's Absence -  Employees Know Who Is in Charge (26 TAC §746.1013(c))

occurrences.finding: Safety - Televisions Anchored to Prevent Tip Over: A television placed on a cart and used for supervised screen time activities was not adequately anchored and risked being tipped over off the cart.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety - Televisions Anchored to Prevent Tip Over (26 TAC §746.3701(10))

occurrences.finding: Mark Cleaning Supplies, Toxic Materials; Keep Separate from Food and Inaccessible to Children: A classroom was observed with cleaning supplies that are within reach of children and not inaccessible.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Mark Cleaning Supplies, Toxic Materials; Keep Separate from Food and Inaccessible to Children (26 TAC §746.3407(12))

occurrences.finding: Written Activity Plans - Plan Followed by Caregiver: The currently available activity plan for the prek classrooms which has toddlers and pre-k age children combined, does not accurately reflect the current activities being provided.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Activity Plans - Plan Followed by Caregiver (26 TAC §746.2203(b))

occurrences.finding: Basic Requirements for Infants - Prompt Attention to Needs: Observations at inspection demonstrated that staff are not routinely checking diapers to ensure diaper changes are being completed promptly. One child was in care for 80 minutes before their diaper was checked and changed. The diaper was overly full and feces was running down the child's leg.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Basic Requirements for Infants - Prompt Attention to Needs (26 TAC §746.2401(4))

occurrences.finding: Written Activity Plan - Outdoor Play Opportunities: The activity plan for the infant classroom lacks an afternoon opportunity for outdoor play. The current activity plan only displays a morning opportunity for outside play at 10:30 am. Additionally, the afternoon does not include any activities for the infants. The schedule goes from nap time, to snack time and then to dismissal.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Activity Plan - Outdoor Play Opportunities (26 TAC §746.2206(1))

occurrences.finding: Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Use Clear, Positive Statements: A caregiver was communicating to the children in a manner that did not encourage positive statements. The caregiver was instructing children to stop crying after instructing a child to stop unwanted behavior and then telling a child they wouldn't have fallen out of a chair if they didn't sit right.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Use Clear, Positive Statements (26 TAC §746.2803(4)(B))

occurrences.finding: Requirements for Feeding Infants - Other Use of Handwashing Sink: The infant room hand washing sink was observed being used to wash toys.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Requirements for Feeding Infants - Other Use of Handwashing Sink (26 TAC §746.2419(8))

occurrences.finding: Written Activity Plans - Plan Followed by Caregiver: The currently available activity plan for the prek classrooms which has toddlers and pre-k age children combined, does not accurately reflect the current activities being provided.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Activity Plans - Plan Followed by Caregiver (26 TAC §746.2203(b))

occurrences.finding: Child Passenger Safety Seat System - Not expired or damaged in accident: Two vehicles were inspected and there were 6 expired booster seats that are used to transport children in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Child Passenger Safety Seat System - Not expired or damaged in accident (26 TAC §746.5607(b))

occurrences.finding: Written Feeding Instructions - Signed and Dated by Parent or Health-Care Professional: One of the infants lacking complete infant feeding instructions is no longer in care. The other infant's feeding instruction still lacks specifics on how frequent formula requires to be given.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Feeding Instructions - Signed and Dated by Parent or Health-Care Professional (26 TAC §746.2421(a))

occurrences.finding: Basic Requirements for Infants - Prompt Attention to Needs: Observations at inspection demonstrated that staff are not routinely checking diapers to ensure diaper changes are being completed promptly.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Basic Requirements for Infants - Prompt Attention to Needs (26 TAC §746.2401(4))

occurrences.finding: Requirements for Feeding Infants - High Chair Trays Sanitized: The high chairs in the infant room were rinsed with water but were not sanitized with a sanitizing product before use.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Requirements for Feeding Infants - High Chair Trays Sanitized (26 TAC §746.2419(9))

occurrences.finding: Employee Handwashing After Handling or Cleaning Bodily Fluids: Staff were observed at inspection cleaning multiple children's noses and not washing their hands afterwards.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Employee Handwashing After Handling or Cleaning Bodily Fluids (26 TAC §746.3415(7))

occurrences.finding: Floors, ceilings and Walls in Good Repair and Clean: The walking babies classroom floor has been cleaned and in better condition. The pre k classroom bathroom still requires to be cleaned to remove dirt and debri from around the toilet. The infant classroom carpet has less debri on the floor but there were staples that infants picked up and almost placed in their mouth. The infant toys still require cleaning.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Floors, ceilings and Walls in Good Repair and Clean (26 TAC §746.3407(9))

occurrences.finding: Written Activity Plans - Plan Followed by Caregiver: The staff were observed at inspection during circle time and art activities in the pre k classroom but the routines observed does not match the written activity plan. Outside time is outlined on the schedule from 8:45 am to 9:15 am but outside time was not observed with nice weather outside. Additionally, the infant schedule does not list their outside opportunities.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Activity Plans - Plan Followed by Caregiver (26 TAC §746.2203(b))

occurrences.finding: Employee Handwashing After Handling or Cleaning Bodily Fluids: Staff were observed at inspection cleaning multiple children's noses and not washing their hands afterwards. Additionally, a staff member cleaned spit up off the carpet and did not wash their own hands afterwards.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Employee Handwashing After Handling or Cleaning Bodily Fluids (26 TAC §746.3415(7))

occurrences.finding: Children Handwashing After Contact with Harmful Substance: A child in care spit up on the carpet and then crawled through the spit up, including their hands coming into direct contact and the staff did not assist the child with appropriate hand washing practices after.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children Handwashing After Contact with Harmful Substance (26 TAC §746.3417(7))

occurrences.finding: Basic Requirements for Infants - Prompt Attention to Needs: Observations at inspection demonstrated that staff are not routinely checking diapers to ensure diaper changes are being completed promptly. One child was in care for over two hours prior to having their diaper checked and changed.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Basic Requirements for Infants - Prompt Attention to Needs (26 TAC §746.2401(4))

occurrences.finding: Written Feeding Instructions - Signed and Dated by Parent or Health-Care Professional: Two infant feeding instructions are lacking clear expectations on infant feeding for the staff to follow. One child's infant feeding instruction does not specify how frequently formula is required and one infant feeding instruction does not provide how many ounces of water or how many scoops of formula is required to provide clear instructions.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Feeding Instructions - Signed and Dated by Parent or Health-Care Professional (26 TAC §746.2421(a))

occurrences.finding: Floors, ceilings and Walls in Good Repair and Clean: Some of the bathrooms floors were cleaned to remove dirt but not al of the floors were cleaned and  were observed to have layered dirt and requires more frequent cleaning practices. Additionally the infant classroom carpet had food crumbs throughout the carpeted area that infants kept picking up and placing in their mouth.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Floors, ceilings and Walls in Good Repair and Clean (26 TAC §746.3407(9))

occurrences.finding: Maintenance Procedures for Active Play - Inspect Daily: The toddler playground was not inspected prior to being used and had various amounts of trash, including a used baby wipe, in the outdoor space used by children in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance Procedures for Active Play - Inspect Daily (26 TAC §746.4751(a))

occurrences.finding: Requirements for Feeding Infants - High Chair Trays Sanitized: The high chairs in the infant room were rinsed with water but were not sanitized with a sanitizing product before use.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Requirements for Feeding Infants - High Chair Trays Sanitized (26 TAC §746.2419(9))

occurrences.finding: Infant Care Area Furnishings and Equipment -Sufficient Number of Toys: Space used for infants during morning drop off routines is not set up to ensure there are sufficient number of toys for infants, including offering a variety of different developmental ranges.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Infant Care Area Furnishings and Equipment -Sufficient Number of Toys (26 TAC §746.2405(5))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know children's names and ages: When various classrooms were combined for morning drop off time, there was not a list of the children's names and ages available to review again at inspection. Once children transitioned to their classrooms two classrooms did not have a list of information of the children's ages they were responsible for.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know children's names and ages (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(3))

occurrences.finding: Requirements for Feeding Infants - Other Use of Handwashing Sink: Based on evidence obtained during the inspection, the hand washing sink in the infant classroom is being used to routinely clean toys that children have placed in their mouth.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Requirements for Feeding Infants - Other Use of Handwashing Sink (26 TAC §746.2419(8))

occurrences.finding: Furnishings and Equipment for Toddlers - Enough Available to Prevent Competition: Toddlers are not provided enough variety of activities, including low shelving for easily accessing the selection of toys during the morning drop off time, so the children are having to compete for the toys that are available.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Furnishings and Equipment for Toddlers - Enough Available to Prevent Competition (26 TAC §746.2505(2))

occurrences.finding: Toys and Equipment to be Sanitized Set Aside: Based on the evidence obtained during the investigation, caregivers are not routinely placing toys aside for sanitizing after a child has placed the toy in their mouth.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Toys and Equipment to be Sanitized Set Aside (26 TAC §746.3407(1))

occurrences.finding: Written Feeding Instructions - Signed and Dated by Parent or Health-Care Professional: An infant in care is lacking infant feeding instructions. An additional infant in care has an infant feeding instruction form signed by the parent but does not provide any direct instructions on what the infant requires for feeding times, the quantity or the frequency expected to be provided by the staff.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Feeding Instructions - Signed and Dated by Parent or Health-Care Professional (26 TAC §746.2421(a))

occurrences.finding: Floors, ceilings and Walls in Good Repair and Clean: The floors of the bathrooms were observed to have layered dirt and requires more frequent cleaning practices.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Floors, ceilings and Walls in Good Repair and Clean (26 TAC §746.3407(9))

occurrences.finding: Illness Preventing Care - Symptoms of Possible Severe Illness: Based on evidence obtained during the investigation, children are being admitted into care when they have symptoms of illness that should exclude them from care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Illness Preventing Care - Symptoms of Possible Severe Illness (26 TAC §746.3601(3)(E))

occurrences.finding: Basic Requirements for Infants - Prompt Attention to Needs: Based on evidence obtained during the investigation, infants are not having their diapers changed promptly when wet. Additionally, the different areas used for infants during morning drop off times does not have a diaper changing area available to ensure infants diapering  needs are being promptly addressed.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Basic Requirements for Infants - Prompt Attention to Needs (26 TAC §746.2401(4))

occurrences.finding: Food Service and Preparation Requirement - No Foods That Present Choking Risk: Food items that present a choking hazard were observed being served to infants at inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Food Service and Preparation Requirement - No Foods That Present Choking Risk (26 TAC §746.3317(7))

occurrences.finding: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children: The infants were observed having 7 infants to one caregiver with a specified age group of 12-17 months. The classroom should of had no more than 5 with one caregiver to be in ratio.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children (26 TAC §746.1601)

occurrences.finding: Child/Caregiver Ratio - 12 or Fewer Children: With 12 children in care with one caregiver responsible for these children there were 3 infants  included in the count of the 12 children and was over ratio.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Child/Caregiver Ratio - 12 or Fewer Children (26 TAC §746.1701)

occurrences.finding: Written Activity Plan-  Screen Time Activities: Children were not offered an alternative activity to screen time when combined for morning drop off. There were no available toys, activities or centers for any of the children ranging from infants to pre k to engage in a different activity.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Activity Plan-  Screen Time Activities (26 TAC §746.2205(b))

occurrences.finding: Screen Time Activities - Not Used for Under Two: Children were observed watching a movie with a combination of ages, including children less than the age of 2.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Screen Time Activities - Not Used for Under Two (26 TAC §746.2207(a))

occurrences.finding: Child/Caregiver Ratio - 18 Months Difference in Age: When the infants were combined with older children, there were 15 children with two caregivers with more than an 18 month age gap between the 4 month old infant and the five year old child grouped together. Additionally when the infants split off into their designated classroom, they then initially had five infants with the youngest 4 months and the oldest 25 months and there continued to be greater than an 18 month age gap until teh 25 month old child was removed to another classroom.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Child/Caregiver Ratio - 18 Months Difference in Age (26 TAC §746.1605(1))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know children's names and ages: When various classrooms were combined for morning drop off time, there was not a list of the children's names and ages available to review. Once children transitioned to their classrooms two classrooms did not have a list of information of the children's ages they were responsible for.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know children's names and ages (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(3))

occurrences.finding: Nutrition and Food Service - Water served safe and sanitary: Staff directed children to the bathroom to drink water from the hand washing sink. The children then went and drank the water from the faucet.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Nutrition and Food Service - Water served safe and sanitary (26 TAC §746.3301(f)(2))

occurrences.finding: Children Handwashing After Toileting or Diapering: Children were observed going to the bathroom to potty and were not washing their hands afterwards.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children Handwashing After Toileting or Diapering (26 TAC §746.3417(3))

occurrences.finding: Written Activity Plans - Plan Followed by Caregiver: Based on evidence obtained during the investigation, staff are not following the written activity plan, including omitting outside activities when the weather is appropriate for outdoor activities.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Activity Plans - Plan Followed by Caregiver (26 TAC §746.2203(b))

occurrences.finding: Personal use of electronic devices, such as cell phones, MP3 players, tablets, and video games: Based on the evidence obtained during the staff are routinely on their cell phones for personal use while supervising children in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Personal use of electronic devices, such as cell phones, MP3 players, tablets, and video games (26 TAC §746.1203(3)(D))

occurrences.finding: Children's Records - Admission Information: A child in care was missing admission information as required.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Records - Admission Information (26 TAC §746.603(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: Written Personnel Policies: Personnel policies related to staff being ill not having direct access to children in care is not being adhered to. A staff member at inspection stated they had to come to work sick and was working in a classroom with children in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Personnel Policies (26 TAC §746.201(2))

occurrences.finding: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment: Various classrooms had areas that require attention related to maintenance. One classroom had outlet overs missing, a broken shelf that is only partially secured to the wall and the trash can with food debri did not have a lid to keep it inaccessible to children in care. Another classroom also had missing outlet covers, a step stool used by children had layered dirt on the top and the sides of the plastic and the bathroom toilet dispenser cover was broken and removed from the wall.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment (26 TAC §746.3407)

occurrences.finding: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric first aid with rescue breathing and choking.: One caregiver did not renew their CPR and First aid certificate promptly prior to the credential expiring on 11/5/2023.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric first aid with rescue breathing and choking. (26 TAC §746.1315(a))

occurrences.finding: Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: A caregiver was observed at inspection communicating to the children in a manner that does not promote positive guidance and praise.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior (26 TAC §746.2803(4)(C))

occurrences.finding: Equipment Prohibited for Younger Than 5 Yrs -Free Standing Arch Climbers: Active play equipment was added onto the playground for infants and toddlers. The climbing equipment are pallets used to form a triangle for climbing up one side and down the other. This free standing arch climber is considered prohibited equipment for children less than 5 years of age.  The climbing equipment are pallets used to form a triangle for climbing up one side and down the other. The pallets are not sanded and have pieces of the wood that is splintered where the children grasp the pieces of wood to climb. Additionally, the climbing equipment lacks loose fill within the 6 foot use zone.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Equipment Prohibited for Younger Than 5 Yrs -Free Standing Arch Climbers (26 TAC §746.4605(a)(1))

occurrences.finding: Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: Another caregiver was observed at inspection communicating to the children in a manner that does not promote positive guidance and praise.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior (26 TAC §746.2803(4)(C))

occurrences.finding: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment: Building and Grounds: Toys were observed at inspection being visibly dirty. Staff interviewed stated that the equipment is still only being sprayed with sanitizer product but is not being wiped clean to remove dirt and debris from the surface of the toys. Toys had visible dirt on them, including large legos blocks, toy trucks and toys meant to be stepped on for balance indoors. The dust was cleaned off the top of the play kitchen and the bouncer was cleaned in the infant classroom. However, there is still a majority of toys in the toddler classroom that have visible dirt on them.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment (26 TAC §746.3407)

occurrences.finding: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment: Toys were observed at inspection being visibly dirty. The equipment was being sprayed with sanitizer product but is not being wiped clean to remove dirt and debris from the surface of the toys. The potty chairs were observed being poured out but not sanitized after each use. There was still visible feces on the side of the potty bowl.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment (26 TAC §746.3407)

occurrences.finding: Care Requirements for Toddlers - Holding and Comforting: A toddler caregiver had various opportunities to offer comfort and support when children were upset and instead, she told them to stop crying.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Care Requirements for Toddlers - Holding and Comforting (26 TAC §746.2501(4))

occurrences.finding: Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: A caregiver was observed at inspection communicating to the children in a manner that does not promote positive guidance and praise.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior (26 TAC §746.2803(4)(C))

occurrences.finding: Employee Handwashing After Diapering a Child: A caregiver was observed at inspection changing consecutive diapers with changing her gloves in between but was not washing her hands.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Employee Handwashing After Diapering a Child (26 TAC §746.3415(4))

occurrences.finding: Diaper Changing Equipment - If Above Floor Level Caregiver Must Face Child and Be Within Arm's Length of Child: A caregiver was observed at inspection leaving a child on the diaper changing station to attend to children in the bathroom. The caregiver did not have their hand on the child and also was not within an arm's length of the child on the diaper changing station.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Diaper Changing Equipment - If Above Floor Level Caregiver Must Face Child and Be Within Arm's Length of Child (26 TAC §746.3503(c)(3))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling: Various children were observed having their arm grabbed when escorting them to time out in a rough manner. Additionally, a child was pushed back against the corner of a shelf in a rough manner when they attempted to get up from time out.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling (26 TAC §746.2805(3))

occurrences.finding: Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Brief Supervised Separation: Several two years were observed being placed in time out for 10 minutes instead of the required one minute the year of their age.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Brief Supervised Separation (26 TAC §746.2803(4)(D))
